xratu 1.5.0 — review what the agent changed, hunk by hunk.

**The headline: a hunk-level review surface.** Until now, seeing what a run
actually changed meant either trusting the transcript's summary or restoring
a checkpoint blind. Every user message that carries a shadow checkpoint now
has a **Review changes** button beside its restore icon, and there's an
**Xratu: Review Changes…** command in the palette. The flow is three picks:
a checkpoint → a changed file → a hunk, and VS Code's native side-by-side
diff opens landed exactly on that chunk of the new side. The button reviews
"since this message"; the command lets you pick any checkpoint and walks the
working tree from there.

The data comes from where it always should have: the shadow git store that
already snapshots before every send. Two new reads power it — a checkpoint
vs. working-tree listing (numstat **plus** the untracked files a run created,
the same blind spot that once made restore silently no-op) and `git show` of
one side at that checkpoint. Nothing ever touches your real repository. The
hunk list itself reuses the line-matcher the approval card already trusted,
flattened for the picker: 1-based starts, ±counts, and a one-line sample of
what changed.

Guard rails first, polish second: binary files are detected before any
preview would be built (numstat for tracked files, a head peek for new
ones — an image never reaches the virtual-document diff), sides larger than
1MB get their own message instead of a giant fake preview, identical sides
say so, and a diff too large for the line-matcher falls back to the
whole-file diff rather than pretending nothing changed. The whole thing is
covered from three directions: unit tests on both new data reads, a unit
test on the hunk flattening, and a browser test that the button posts the
row's checkpoint to the host (verified by screenshot, sidebar width).

**The house got a spring clean, with the furniture in the same places.**
The two god files were split along seams they already had:
`localAgent.ts` (the agent loop) went from 4,315 lines to seven files, and
`extension.ts` went from 7,512 lines to 6,145 with its ~60-case webview
message router lifted into its own module. This is a pure move — the public
surface of `localAgent.ts` was verified name-for-name against the compiled
module before and after (55/55 identical), the router's switch runs against
an interface the provider explicitly implements so the compiler checks every
member, and the three tests that pinned the old file layout were re-pointed
exactly as their own failure messages instructed. If a behavior changed, the
65 host suites, the protocol-drift guard, or the 132 browser tests would
have caught it; all of them are green on Windows, macOS and Linux.

**Developer work you'll only ever feel as fewer bugs.** Lint now encodes the
project's non-negotiable rules as AST checks (process killing, no shell
strings, CSS logical properties), the host test suite dropped from minutes
to ~14 seconds with parallel workers (serial on Windows, deliberately), and
the host↔webview message protocol is guarded both ways so a renamed message
fails CI instead of failing at runtime. Releases also publish themselves
now: pushing a `v*` tag builds the VSIX and attaches it to the GitHub
Release — no manual upload step.

Version 1.4.2 → 1.5.0. As always: BYOK, everything local, your credentials
never leave VS Code's secret storage.
